newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gehe still eyes Lloyds Chemists.
newsitem.headline: Gehe still eyes Lloyds Chemists.

text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG said on Monday it remained interested in acquiring UK drugs chain Lloyds Chemists Plc but declined to give any information on possible plans to launch a new bid.
"Our interest in Lloyds Chemists remains unchanged, but I cannot comment further on our plans," Gehe Chief Financial Officer Karl-Gerhard Eick told Reuters in answer to an enquiry.
The Financial Times, in its Monday edition, wrote that Gehe will likely launch a new bid topping its rival UniChem Plc's offer made in October this week.

On October 18 UniChem submitted a bid valuing Lloyds Chemists at 657.6 million stg. For every 10 Lloyds Chemists shares UniChem is offering 16 new UniChem shares and 926 p in cash, valuing each Lloyds Chemists share at 505.4 p.
The newspaper wrote a Gehe bid of 505 p a share is likely and that the group may offer as much as 525 p a share.
Eick declined all comment on any possible bid price.
But he said the group would take a decision this week to meet a deadline set by the U.K. government when it approved Gehe and UniChem's plans to sell off some of Lloyds Chemists units.
"We will make a decision this week because we have to," Eick said, adding this would be officially announced.
Gehe closed Frankfurt bourse trade down 50 pfennigs at 101.50 on Friday.
